notes: Mark FC when multiple pops occur close together; hold settings. Don't increase heat to chase a brief FC dip. Decaf: FC comes early (about 182-187) and quieter than regular beans.

history.change: Initial procedure, copied from Honduran MWP Decaf (current version): charge burner 45 / SV 230; burner 40 at 150, 35 + air 40 at 175, 30 at 189, 25 at 196; drop at 202.8. The reference is #29 (Honduran MWP, the same steps); there is no roast of this bean yet.
history.why: Untried bean, so this starts from the most similar one with history. Burman's Decaffeinated Colombian Royal Select MWP (part of the 3 lb decaf bundle; Burman Coffee order #335002 (2026-10-14), 1 lb, 3 batches): Colombian beans, Mountain Water Process at a dedicated plant in Mexico. Lower acidity and sweeter: full body, chocolate and roasted walnut, a mellow sweet finish; floral hints when light, smoke and spice when dark. Burman calls it versatile and says to avoid cinnamon (very light) roast points with decaf. The listing gives no region, variety, altitude or screen size. Honduran MWP Decaf is the closest match on every count: the same Royal Select MWP line from the same plant, and its 202.8 drop made an excellent latte (#29) and a REALLY GOOD half-caf latte (#34), which is what the decafs are for. Colombian coffee is usually grown higher than Honduran (often 1,400-1,900 m), so it may be denser and reach FC a little later than #29's 6:48; if so, keep the drop temperature and let the time stretch. Decafs crack earlier and quieter than regular beans (FC at 182-187 in the Honduran roasts). First guess; adjust after tasting.
